verses.1: Then Pilate took Jesus and brought him out.
verses.2: And the soldiers, after wearing wreaths made of hair, laid them upon his head. They also covered him with a cloth made of purple fabric.
verses.3: And they came forward to him and said, “Hail, king of the Jews!” And they gave him gifts.
verses.4: And Pilate once again went out and said to them, “Let me take him out before you, so that you can see that I find no reason to condemn him.”
verses.5: So, Jesus came out, wearing the crown of thorns and a purple robe. He said to them, “This is the man.”
verses.6: When the high priests and their assistants saw him, they cried out, “Kneel down and be crucified!” Pilate said to them, “Take him yourselves and crucify him. I don’t find any fault in him.”
verses.7: The Jews replied to him, “We have laws. And according to those laws, he must die, because he created himself as the son of God.”
verses.8: And when Pilate heard these words, he became even more afraid.
verses.9: And he entered the palace again and said to Jesus, “Where are you?” But Jesus did not answer him.
verses.10: So, Pilate says to him, “Do you not speak? Do you not know that I have power to set you free, and also to crucify you?”
verses.11: Jesus said to him, “You had no authority over me unless it were given you from above. Therefore, the one who handed you over to me has greater sin on his own shoulders.”
verses.12: Therefore, Pilate wanted to execute him. But the Jews cried out, saying, “If you execute him, you are not a friend of the Emperor. Every king who makes himself king against the will of the Emperor is considered an enemy of the Emperor.”
verses.13: So, after hearing these words from Pilate, he brought Jesus out. He sat down on a place called Lystra, which was a Hebrew term for “Gabbaoth”.
verses.14: It was the time of fasting; it was about the eighth hour. He said to the Jews, “Look, your king is coming.”
verses.15: So they cried out, “Holy God, crucify him!” Pilate said to them, “Will I crucify your king?” The priests replied, “We have no king except Caesar.”
verses.16: Then he gave him to them so that he could be crucified. We therefore took Jesus away.
verses.17: And while he was bearing the cross upon himself, he went to what is called Kraniou Tópion. It is said that this place was founded by the Hebrew Golgotha.
verses.18: Where they tied him up, and along with him, two others were also tied in the same way, right in the middle of Jesus.
verses.19: Pilato also wrote a title on the cross. It read: “Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews.”
verses.20: So, many Jews interpreted this title as meaning that the place where Jesus was crucified was a sacred site. It was also written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin.
verses.21: So, the high priests of the Jews said to Pilate, “Do not write ‘King of the Jews’. It should be written ‘I am the King of the Jews’.”
verses.22: Pilatos said nothing; I wrote what I wrote.
verses.23: So, when the soldiers raised Jesus in triumph, they took His clothes and divided them into four parts. Each soldier received one part of the clothes, along with a blanket. The blanket itself was made of wool; it had a hood that covered part of its surface.
verses.24: So they said to each other: “Let us not harm him. Instead, let us discuss what should be done regarding him, so that the writing can be fulfilled as it is meant.” They divided my clothes among themselves and put a crown on my head. These soldiers did these things.
verses.25: Also present near the cross of Jesus were his mother and her sister, Mary Magdalene and Mary the daughter of Klopas.
verses.26: Jesus, seeing the mother and the disciple, said to her, “Behold, your son!”
verses.27: Then he said to his disciple, “Come, your mother.” And from her, the disciple received her immediately.
verses.28: After this, Jesus knew that everything was already finished, so that the writing could be completed. He said, “I have completed it.”
verses.29: The instrument was made of a suitable material. So, they took the suitable material and placed it inside the mouth of the instrument, thereby fitting it into that opening.
verses.30: When Jesus received his baptism, he said, “It is finished.” Then the Spirit placed a crown on His head.
verses.31: The Jews, since they wanted to avoid staying on the cross during Sunday, as it was a very important day on that Sunday, asked Pilate to allow them to remove their shoes before standing on the cross.
verses.32: So, the soldiers came. They cut off the hair from the first one, and from the other ones who were tied up with ropes.
verses.33: But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he had already died, they did not remove his clothes.
verses.34: But one of the soldiers pulled up his sword, and immediately blood and water came out from it.
verses.35: And He who was the witness also testified. His testimony is true indeed. He knew that what he said was true, so that you too might believe.
verses.36: For this is what must happen in order for the writing to be fulfilled. Then, it will not be destroyed by him.
verses.37: And again, another statement is made: They will see whom they have chosen.
verses.38: After that, Joseph of Arimathea asked Pilate to allow him to see the body of Jesus. He was a disciple of Jesus, but he was kept hidden because of the Jews’ fears. Pilate allowed it. So, Joseph went and saw the body of Jesus.
verses.39: And Nicodemus also came, the first person to visit him at night, carrying mixtures of smyrnium and aloes, amounting to one hundred liters each.
verses.40: So they received the body of Jesus, and they also gave it to the angels along with the spices, as is the custom among the Jews when burying a person.
verses.41: And there was a garden in that place where he was crucified. In that garden, there was also a monument to his memory. But no one had ever been allowed to visit that place before.
verses.42: Therefore, due to the preparations made by the Jews, since the tomb was small in size, they placed Jesus there.
